     6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.PicRepColimitCompat
     7	import Mathlib.FieldTheory.SeparableClosure
     8	
     9	/-!
    10	# DAT-G0 β1 — the base-field directed system `K_s = colim k''` (DG-G0.δ) and the pinned residual
    11	
    12	This file lands **DG-G0.δ** (mini-spec `informal/spec-datg0.md` §3, landing notes I-0259/I-0263):
    13	the base-field directed system whose colimit is the separable closure `K_s`, over which the
    14	β1 residual `Pic0PreservesFilteredBaseColimit` (landed in `Picard/PicRepColimitCompat.lean`,
    15	commit c9df8d479) is quantified.
    16	
    17	## DG-G0.δ — the substrate the residual quantifies over
    18	
    19	For a **separable algebraic** extension `K/k` (the case `K = K_s` a separable closure is the
    20	DAT-G0 target), the finite subextensions form a **directed system** whose supremum is all of
    21	`K`.  Concretely:
    22	
    23	* `FinSubext k K` — the index: finite(-dimensional) `k`-subextensions `k''` of `K`, ordered by
    24	  inclusion.  It is **nonempty** and **directed** (`instNonemptyFinSubext`,
    25	  `directed_finSubext`), so `(FinSubext k K)ᵒᵖ` is `IsCofiltered` — the shape the residual's
    26	  `[IsCofiltered J]` binder consumes.
    27	* `iSup_finSubext_eq_top` — `⨆ k'', k'' = ⊤`, i.e. **`K = colim k''`** at the lattice level.
    28	* `coe_iSup_finSubext` — the colimit-is-**union** identity `↑(⨆ k'', k'') = ⋃ k'', ↑k''`
    29	  (`IntermediateField.coe_iSup_of_directed`): every element of `K` already lives at a finite
    30	  stage.  This is the honest content of "`K_s = colim k''`": the test-scheme limit
    31	  `S_{K_s} = lim S_{k''}` is `Spec` of this filtered colimit of fields.
    32	* `isSeparable_finSubext` — every stage `k''/k` is **separable** (`Algebra.IsSeparable`,
    33	  inherited from `K/k` by `Algebra.isSeparable_tower_bot_of_isSeparable`); with
    34	  `IntermediateField.isSeparable_iSup` the colimit is separable, so this is genuinely the
    35	  system of *finite separable* subextensions of `K_s/k`.
    36	
    37	All native `k`-algebra / scalar-tower instances come from the `IntermediateField` API
    38	(`Algebra k k''`, `IsScalarTower k k'' K`), per the I-0255 tower-diamond wall — no composite
    39	`RingHom.toAlgebra` `letI`s are built here.
    40	
    41	## The β1 residual (pinned — `Pic0PreservesFilteredBaseColimit`, in `PicRepColimitCompat`)
    42	
    43	The β1 reduction is LANDED (`PicRepColimitCompat.lean`, c9df8d479): the base-field-change
    44	functoriality of `pic0` is the landed natural iso `pic0ThetaType`, collapsing the varying-field
    45	colimit onto the single fixed functor `pic0TypeFunctor C` over `k`, whose base-field-colimit
    46	compatibility is the named `Prop`
    47	
    48	```
    49	Pic0PreservesFilteredBaseColimit C :=
    50	  ∀ ⦃J⦄ [SmallCategory J] [IsCofiltered J] (S : J ⥤ Over (Spec (.of k))),
    51	    (∀ f, IsAffineHom (S.map f).left) → (∀ i, CompactSpace (S.obj i).left) →
    52	    (∀ i, QuasiSeparatedSpace (S.obj i).left) → ∀ [HasLimit S],
    53	      PreservesColimit S.op (pic0TypeFunctor C)
    54	```
    55	
    56	`instConsumesFiniteBaseColimit` below records that this `Prop` **applies to** the δ system:
    57	`(FinSubext k K)ᵒᵖ` is `IsCofiltered`, so any cofiltered diagram `S` of test schemes indexed by
    58	it (in particular the `Spec`-of-tests limit `S_{K_s} = lim_{k''} S_{k''}`) is a legal input.
    59	
    60	**The residual proper is NOT discharged here** — it is genuinely M–L (I-0263): it says
    61	`pic0TypeFunctor C` is *locally of finite presentation as a functor*, which on affine tests
    62	`overSpec k A` is exactly that the affine relative-Picard construction `PicEtAff C A` commutes
    63	with filtered colimits of the test algebra `A`, riding finite presentation of the proper smooth
    64	curve `C/k`.  The precise remaining goal state and its named mathlib avatars
    65	(`CommRingCat.preservesColimit_coyoneda_of_finitePresentation`,
    66	`Scheme.exists_π_app_comp_eq_of_locallyOfFinitePresentation`, …) are pinned in the
    67	`PicRepColimitCompat` module docstring and landing note I-0263; this file lands the δ substrate
    68	they act on and leaves the analytic core `sorry`-free-pinned (no `sorry` in this file).
    69	-/
    70	
    71	set_option autoImplicit false
    72	
    73	universe u
    74	
    75	open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite IntermediateField
    76	
    77	namespace AlgebraicGeometry.DatG0
    78	
    79	/-! ## DG-G0.δ — the base-field directed system `K_s = colim k''` -/
    80	
    81	section FieldSystem
    82	
    83	variable (k K : Type u) [Field k] [Field K] [Algebra k K]
    84	
    85	/-- **The DG-G0.δ index** — the finite subextensions `k''` of a separable algebraic extension
    86	`K/k`, ordered by inclusion.  Its directed supremum is `K` (`iSup_finSubext_eq_top`); its
    87	opposite is the `IsCofiltered` shape the β1 residual `Pic0PreservesFilteredBaseColimit`
    88	quantifies over.  For `K = K_s` a separable closure these are exactly the *finite separable*
    89	subextensions of `K_s/k`. -/
    90	abbrev FinSubext : Type u := {L : IntermediateField k K // FiniteDimensional k L}
    91	
    92	variable {k K}
    93	
    94	/-- Each stage carries its finite-dimensionality as an instance. -/
    95	instance (L : FinSubext k K) : FiniteDimensional k L.1 := L.2
    96	
    97	variable (k K) in
    98	/-- The δ index is nonempty (`k` itself, as `⊥`, is a finite subextension). -/
    99	instance instNonemptyFinSubext [Algebra.IsAlgebraic k K] : Nonempty (FinSubext k K) :=
   100	  ⟨⟨k⟮(0 : K)⟯, adjoin.finiteDimensional (Algebra.IsIntegral.isIntegral _)⟩⟩
   101	
   102	/-- **DG-G0.δ, directedness.**  The finite subextensions of `K/k` are directed under inclusion:
   103	the join `k'' ⊔ k'''` of two finite subextensions is again finite.  Hence `(FinSubext k K)ᵒᵖ` is
   104	`IsCofiltered` — the shape the residual consumes. -/
   105	theorem directed_finSubext :
   106	    Directed (· ≤ ·) (fun L : FinSubext k K => (L.1 : IntermediateField k K)) := by
   107	  intro L₁ L₂
   108	  haveI := L₁.2
   109	  haveI := L₂.2
   110	  exact ⟨⟨L₁.1 ⊔ L₂.1, IntermediateField.finiteDimensional_sup _ _⟩, le_sup_left, le_sup_right⟩
   111	
   112	/-- **DG-G0.δ, `IsDirected`.**  The δ index is a directed order (from `directed_finSubext`), so it
   113	is `IsFiltered` and its opposite `(FinSubext k K)ᵒᵖ` is `IsCofiltered` — automatically, via
   114	`isFiltered_of_directed_le_nonempty` and `isCofiltered_op_of_isFiltered`. -/
   115	instance instIsDirectedFinSubext [Algebra.IsAlgebraic k K] :
   116	    IsDirected (FinSubext k K) (· ≤ ·) :=
   117	  ⟨fun L₁ L₂ => directed_finSubext L₁ L₂⟩
   118	
   119	/-- **DG-G0.δ, the cofiltered shape the residual consumes.**  `(FinSubext k K)ᵒᵖ` is
   120	`IsCofiltered` — exactly the `[IsCofiltered J]` shape of `Pic0PreservesFilteredBaseColimit`'s
   121	diagram binder.  A cofiltered diagram of test schemes `S : (FinSubext k K)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Over (Spec k)`
   122	indexed by it — in particular the `Spec`-of-tests limit `S_{K_s} = lim_{k''} S_{k''}` (with
   123	affine transition maps `Spec k''' → Spec k''` and one-point, hence compact and quasi-separated,
   124	stages) — is therefore a legal input to the β1 residual. -/
   125	instance instIsCofilteredFinSubextOp [Algebra.IsAlgebraic k K] :
   126	    IsCofiltered (FinSubext k K)ᵒᵖ :=
   127	  inferInstance
   128	
   129	/-- **DG-G0.δ, the colimit at the lattice level: `K = colim k''`.**  For an algebraic extension
   130	`K/k` the supremum of the finite subextensions is all of `K`: every `x : K` is algebraic, hence
   131	lies in the finite subextension `k⟮x⟯`. -/
   132	theorem iSup_finSubext_eq_top [Algebra.IsAlgebraic k K] :
   133	    ⨆ L : FinSubext k K, (L.1 : IntermediateField k K) = ⊤ :=
   134	  le_top.antisymm fun x _ =>
   135	    le_iSup (fun L : FinSubext k K => (L.1 : IntermediateField k K))
   136	      ⟨k⟮x⟯, adjoin.finiteDimensional (Algebra.IsIntegral.isIntegral x)⟩ <|
   137	      mem_adjoin_simple_self k x
   138	
   139	/-- **DG-G0.δ, colimit-is-union.**  The directed supremum of the finite subextensions is their
   140	set-theoretic **union** (`IntermediateField.coe_iSup_of_directed`): the honest "`K_s = colim k''`"
   141	statement.  Combined with `iSup_finSubext_eq_top`, every element of `K` already lives at a finite
   142	stage `k''`. -/
   143	theorem coe_iSup_finSubext [Algebra.IsAlgebraic k K] :
   144	    (↑(⨆ L : FinSubext k K, (L.1 : IntermediateField k K)) : Set K)
   145	      = ⋃ L : FinSubext k K, (L.1 : Set K) :=
   146	  IntermediateField.coe_iSup_of_directed directed_finSubext
   147	
   148	/-- **DG-G0.δ, separability of each stage.**  Every finite subextension `k''/k` of a separable
   149	extension `K/k` is itself separable (`Algebra.isSeparable_tower_bot_of_isSeparable` on the native
   150	tower `k → k'' → K`).  With `IntermediateField.isSeparable_iSup` the colimit `⨆ k''` is separable,
   151	so the δ system is the directed system of *finite separable* subextensions. -/
   152	instance isSeparable_finSubext [Algebra.IsSeparable k K] (L : FinSubext k K) :
   153	    Algebra.IsSeparable k L.1 :=
   154	  Algebra.isSeparable_tower_bot_of_isSeparable k L.1 K
   155	
   156	end FieldSystem
   157	
   158	end AlgebraicGeometry.DatG0

    12	/-!
    13	# The separably closed Picard representer as Jacobian data
    14	
    15	The admissible Abel chart is etale-locally surjective onto the exact representing
    16	scheme obtained from the separably closed Picard construction.  Its quasi-compact
    17	divisor source therefore supplies quasi-compactness of that exact carrier, which
    18	packages into `PicRepDatum` and then `JacobianData` without changing the carrier or
    19	its representation.
    20	-/
    21	
    22	set_option autoImplicit false
    23	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
    24	
    25	universe u
    26	
    27	open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory
    28	
    29	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    30	
    31	attribute [local instance] Over.sectionsAlgebra Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra
    32	attribute [local instance 10000] relCurve.instOver
    33	
    34	variable {k : Type u} [Field k]
    35	
    36	noncomputable section
    37	
    38	/-- Etale-local surjectivity of a Yoneda map is surjectivity on the underlying points. -/
    39	theorem surjective_of_isLocallySurjective_yoneda_map {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    40	    (h : Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.etaleTopology (yoneda.map f)) :
    41	    Function.Surjective f.base := by
    42	  intro y
    43	  let s : ToType ((yoneda.obj Y).obj (op (Spec (Y.residueField y)))) :=
    44	    Y.fromSpecResidueField y
    45	  have hmem := h.imageSieve_mem s
    46	  obtain ⟨cover, hcover⟩ :=
    47	    (Scheme.mem_grothendieckTopology_iff (P := @Etale)).mp hmem
    48	  obtain ⟨r⟩ := (inferInstance : Nonempty (PrimeSpectrum (Y.residueField y)))
    49	  obtain ⟨i, z, hz⟩ := cover.exists_eq r
    50	  have hi : (Presieve.ofArrows cover.X cover.f) (cover.f i) := ⟨i⟩
    51	  obtain ⟨q, hq⟩ := hcover (cover.X i) (cover.f i) hi
    52	  change q ≫ f = cover.f i ≫ Y.fromSpecResidueField y at hq
    53	  refine ⟨q.base z, ?_⟩
    54	  have hqz := congrArg (fun g : cover.X i ⟶ Y => g.base z) hq
    55	  change f.base (q.base z) = (Y.fromSpecResidueField y).base ((cover.f i).base z) at hqz
    56	  rw [hz, Scheme.fromSpecResidueField_apply] at hqz
    57	  exact hqz

    43	/-! ## Sigma-extension isomorphisms -/
    44	
    45	/-- Sigma extension preserves natural isomorphisms of slice presheaves. -/
    46	noncomputable def sigmaExtensionIso {F G : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    47	    (e : F ≅ G) :
    48	    Over.sigmaExtension (Spec (.of k)) F ≅
    49	      Over.sigmaExtension (Spec (.of k)) G where
    50	  hom := Over.sigmaExtensionNat e.hom
    51	  inv := Over.sigmaExtensionNat e.inv
    52	  hom_inv_id := by
    53	    ext T x
    54	    rcases x with ⟨a, x⟩
    55	    exact congrArg (Sigma.mk a) (e.hom_inv_id_app_apply _ x)
    56	  inv_hom_id := by
    57	    ext T x
    58	    rcases x with ⟨a, x⟩
    59	    exact congrArg (Sigma.mk a) (e.inv_hom_id_app_apply _ x)
    60	
    61	/-- A representation on the slice extends to an isomorphism between the ambient Yoneda
    62	presheaf of its representing object and the sigma extension. -/
    63	noncomputable def representableBySigmaIso
    64	    {F : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} {J : Over (Spec (.of k))}
    65	    (rep : F.RepresentableBy J) :
    66	    yoneda.obj J.left ≅ Over.sigmaExtension (Spec (.of k)) F where
    67	  hom := rep.toSigmaExtension
    68	  inv :=
    69	    { app := fun T => TypeCat.ofHom fun x => (rep.homEquiv.symm x.2).left
    70	      naturality := by
    71	        intro T T' f
    72	        ext x
    73	        rcases x with ⟨a, x⟩
    74	        let q : Over.mk (f.unop ≫ a) ⟶ Over.mk a := Over.homMk f.unop rfl
    75	        exact (congrArg Over.Hom.left
    76	          (rep.comp_homEquiv_symm x q)).symm }
    77	  hom_inv_id := by
    78	    ext T v
    79	    exact congrArg Over.Hom.left (rep.homEquiv.symm_apply_apply
    80	      (Over.homMk v rfl : Over.mk (v ≫ J.hom) ⟶ J))
    81	  inv_hom_id := by
    82	    ext T x
    83	    rcases x with ⟨a, x⟩
    84	    let g := rep.homEquiv.symm x
    85	    have hga : g.left ≫ J.hom = a := g.w
    86	    refine Over.sigmaExtension_ext F hga ?_
    87	    change F.map (Over.mkCongr hga).op x =
    88	      rep.homEquiv (Over.homMk g.left rfl : Over.mk (g.left ≫ J.hom) ⟶ J)
    89	    rw [← rep.homEquiv.apply_symm_apply x]
    90	    rw [← rep.homEquiv_comp]
    91	    exact congrArg rep.homEquiv (Over.OverMorphism.ext rfl)

    95	/-- The Yoneda range of an open immersion is represented by its source.  Here the range is
    96	identified with the exact divisor predicate whose Abel class lies in `PicRankOneOpen`. -/
    97	noncomputable def rankOneDivisorOpenRepresentableBy
    98	    (pi : C.left ⟶ P1 k) [IsFinite pi]
    99	    (h : DivRankOneOpenData (C := C) pi) :
   100	    (divRankOnePresentationPreimageRepresenter pi).toFunctor.RepresentableBy
   101	      (divRankOneOpenOver pi h) where
   102	  homEquiv {T} :=
   103	    { toFun := fun y => ⟨y ≫ divRankOneOpenOverMap pi h, by
   104	        have hy : y ≫ divRankOneOpenOverMap pi h ∈
   105	            (openSubfunctor (divRepAffGenusScheme C) h.carrier).obj (op T) :=
   106	          ⟨y, rfl⟩
   107	        rw [h.carrier_eq] at hy
   108	        exact hy⟩
   109	      invFun := fun x => Classical.choose
   110	        (rankOneRepresenterRestriction_factorization pi h x)
   111	      left_inv := fun y => by
   112	        apply Over.OverMorphism.ext
   113	        letI : IsOpenImmersion (divRankOneOpenMap pi h) :=
   114	          divRankOneOpen_isOpenImmersion pi h
   115	        apply (cancel_mono (divRankOneOpenMap pi h)).mp
   116	        exact congrArg Over.Hom.left (Classical.choose_spec
   117	          (rankOneRepresenterRestriction_factorization pi h
   118	            ⟨y ≫ divRankOneOpenOverMap pi h, by
   119	              have hy : y ≫ divRankOneOpenOverMap pi h ∈
   120	                  (openSubfunctor (divRepAffGenusScheme C) h.carrier).obj (op T) :=
   121	                ⟨y, rfl⟩
   122	              rw [h.carrier_eq] at hy
   123	              exact hy⟩))
   124	      right_inv := fun x => by
   125	        apply Subtype.ext
   126	        exact Classical.choose_spec
   127	          (rankOneRepresenterRestriction_factorization pi h x) }
   128	  homEquiv_comp {T T'} f y := by
   129	    apply Subtype.ext
   130	    exact Category.assoc f y (divRankOneOpenOverMap pi h)

   156	/-! ## Translation by a base class of degree `genus C` -/
   157	
   158	/-- Base classes which translate degree zero into the genus-degree layer. -/
   159	abbrev PicRankOneTranslatorIndex :=
   160	  {L : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CechPic // classDeg k L = (genus C : ℤ)}
   161	
   162	/-- Multiplication by a translator, at one test object. -/
   163	noncomputable def pic0GenusTranslationEquiv
   164	    (a : PicRankOneTranslatorIndex (C := C)) (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) :
   165	    pic0Subgroup C T ≃ picDegLayer C (genus C : ℤ) T where
   166	  toFun lam := ⟨lam.1 * thetaFamily C a.1 T, fun K _ _ t => by
   167	    rw [degAt_mul, lam.2 K t, degAt_thetaFamily, zero_add, a.2]⟩
   168	  invFun lam := ⟨lam.1 * (thetaFamily C a.1 T)⁻¹,
   169	    mem_pic0Subgroup_iff.mpr fun K _ _ t => by
   170	      rw [degAt_mul, degAt_inv, degAt_thetaFamily, lam.2 K t, a.2]
   171	      ring⟩
   172	  left_inv lam := Subtype.ext (mul_inv_cancel_right _ _)
   173	  right_inv lam := Subtype.ext (inv_mul_cancel_right _ _)
   174	
   175	/-- Multiplication by a translator is the natural isomorphism from `Pic^0` to the genus-degree
   176	Picard layer.  It is the degree-specialized, one-fold form of `mulThetaPowNatIso`. -/
   177	noncomputable def pic0GenusTranslationIso (a : PicRankOneTranslatorIndex (C := C)) :
   178	    pic0TypeFunctor C ≅ picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ) :=
   179	  NatIso.ofComponents (fun T => (pic0GenusTranslationEquiv (C := C) a T.unop).toIso) (by
   180	    intro T T' f
   181	    ext lam
   182	    refine Subtype.ext ?_
   183	    have key :
   184	        picEtMap C f.unop ((pic0Subgroup C T.unop).subtype lam) *
   185	            thetaFamily C a.1 T'.unop =
   186	          picEtMap C f.unop
   187	            ((pic0Subgroup C T.unop).subtype lam * thetaFamily C a.1 T.unop) := by
   188	      rw [map_mul, thetaFamily_natural]
   189	    exact key)

   191	/-! ## The translated rank-one charts -/

   193	/-- The certified divisor open, transported by the canonical Abel isomorphism, represents the
   194	rank-one Picard locus on the big site. -/
   195	noncomputable def picRankOneOpenSigmaIso
   196	    (h : DivRankOneOpenData (C := C) (divRepAffP1Map C)) :
   197	    yoneda.obj (divRankOneOpenOver (divRepAffP1Map C) h).left ≅

   203	/-- The chart indexed by a base class `a` of degree `genus C`: first use canonical Abel on the
   204	rank-one divisor open, then multiply by `a⁻¹` to return to degree zero. -/
   205	noncomputable def picRankOneTranslatedChart
   206	    (h : DivRankOneOpenData (C := C) (divRepAffP1Map C))
   207	    (a : PicRankOneTranslatorIndex (C := C)) :
   208	    yoneda.obj (divRankOneOpenOver (divRepAffP1Map C) h).left ⟶

   210	  (picRankOneOpenSigmaIso (C := C) h).hom ≫
   211	    picRankOneOpenSigmaIncl (divRepAffP1Map C) ≫
   212	      (sigmaExtensionIso (pic0GenusTranslationIso (C := C) a)).inv

   214	/-- Every translated rank-one chart is a representable open immersion. -/
   215	theorem picRankOneTranslatedChart_isOpenImmersion
   216	    (hopen : PicRankOneOpen.IsOpen (divRepAffP1Map C))
   217	    (a : PicRankOneTranslatorIndex (C := C)) :
   218	    IsOpenImmersion.presheaf
   219	      (picRankOneTranslatedChart (C := C)
   220	        (divRankOneOpenDataOfPicRankOneOpen (divRepAffP1Map C) hopen) a) := by
   221	  apply MorphismProperty.IsStableUnderComposition.comp_mem
   222	  · apply MorphismProperty.IsStableUnderComposition.comp_mem
   223	    · exact MorphismProperty.of_isIso (P := IsOpenImmersion.presheaf) _
   224	    · exact MorphismProperty.of_isIso (P := IsOpenImmersion.presheaf) _
   225	  · apply MorphismProperty.IsStableUnderComposition.comp_mem
   226	    · exact hopen
   227	    · exact MorphismProperty.of_isIso (P := IsOpenImmersion.presheaf) _

   231	/-- The chosen genus divisor representer is locally of finite type over the base.  In positive
   232	genus it is definitionally a divisor scheme.  In genus zero, representer uniqueness transports
   233	the certificate from the terminal representer. -/
   234	theorem locallyOfFiniteType_divRepAffGenusScheme :
   235	    LocallyOfFiniteType (divRepAffGenusScheme C).hom := by
   236	  by_cases hg : genus C = 0
   237	  · let D0 : Over (Spec (.of k)) := Over.mk (𝟙 (Spec (.of k)))
   238	    have rep0 : (divFunctorAff C (genus C)).RepresentableBy D0 := by
   239	      rw [hg]

   241	    let e := (divFunctorAff_genus_representableBy C).uniqueUpToIso rep0
   242	    haveI : LocallyOfFiniteType D0.hom := by
   243	      change LocallyOfFiniteType (𝟙 (Spec (.of k)))
   244	      infer_instance
   245	    rw [← Over.w e.hom]
   246	    infer_instance
   247	  · unfold divRepAffGenusScheme divFunctorAffGenusRepresenter divRepAffScheme_at
   248	      divFunctorAffRepresenter_at
   249	    dsimp only
   250	    rw [dif_neg hg]
   251	    infer_instance

   275	/-! ## From residue-field coverage to pointwise coverage -/
   276	
   277	/-- A family of representable open immersions covers pointwise as soon as it covers the class at
   278	every residue-field point.  Relative representability pulls a chosen field factorization back to
   279	an open immersion over the test; its open range is the required neighborhood. -/
   280	theorem pointwiseCoverage_of_residueField
   281	    {I : Type u} {X : I → Scheme.{u}}
   282	    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
   283	    (hf : ∀ i, IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (f i))
   284	    (hfield : ∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (s : (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op T)) (t : T),
   285	      ∃ (Y : Scheme.{u}) (q : Y) (y : Y ⟶ T) (i : I) (x : Y ⟶ X i),
   286	        y.base q = t ∧
   287	          (f i).app (op Y) x = (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.map y.op s) :
   288	    PointwiseCoverage C f := by
   289	  intro T s t
   290	  obtain ⟨Y, q, y, i, x, hyt, hx⟩ := hfield T s t
   291	  let g : yoneda.obj T ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1 := yonedaEquiv.symm s
   292	  obtain ⟨Z, snd, fst, hpb⟩ := (hf i).rep g
   293	  letI : IsOpenImmersion snd := (hf i).property g fst snd hpb
   294	  have hpbY := (IsPullback.iff_app.mp hpb) (op Y)
   295	  rw [Types.isPullback_iff] at hpbY
   296	  have hg : g.app (op Y) y = (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.map y.op s := by
   297	    exact yonedaEquiv_symm_app_apply s _ y
   298	  obtain ⟨z, hz₁, hz₂⟩ := hpbY.2.2 x y (hx.trans hg.symm)
   299	  let W : T.Opens := snd.opensRange
   300	  have htW : t ∈ W := by
   301	    change t ∈ snd.opensRange
   302	    apply Scheme.Hom.mem_opensRange.mpr
   303	    refine ⟨z.base q, ?_⟩
   304	    have hz := congrArg (fun m : Y ⟶ T => m.base q) hz₂
   305	    exact hz.trans hyt
   306	  refine ⟨W, htW, i, fst.app (op (W : Scheme.{u})) snd.isoOpensRange.inv, ?_⟩
   307	  have hpbW := (IsPullback.iff_app.mp hpb) (op (W : Scheme.{u}))
   308	  rw [Types.isPullback_iff] at hpbW
   309	  have hcomm := congrArg
   310	    (fun q => (ConcreteCategory.hom q) snd.isoOpensRange.inv) hpbW.1
   311	  change (f i).app (op (W : Scheme.{u}))
   312	      (fst.app (op (W : Scheme.{u})) snd.isoOpensRange.inv) = _
   313	  change (f i).app (op (W : Scheme.{u}))
   314	      (fst.app (op (W : Scheme.{u})) snd.isoOpensRange.inv) =
   315	    g.app (op (W : Scheme.{u})) (snd.isoOpensRange.inv ≫ snd) at hcomm
   316	  rw [Scheme.Hom.isoOpensRange_inv_comp] at hcomm
   317	  change (f i).app (op (W : Scheme.{u}))
   318	      (fst.app (op (W : Scheme.{u})) snd.isoOpensRange.inv) =
   319	    (yonedaEquiv.symm s).app (op (W : Scheme.{u})) W.ι at hcomm
   320	  rwa [yonedaEquiv_symm_app_apply] at hcomm

   326	/-- Every degree-zero field class is hit by the translated chart indexed by the exact base class
   327	returned by `exists_sepClosedTranslated_mem_picRankOneOpen`. -/
   328	theorem exists_picRankOneTranslatedChart_fieldFactorization
   329	    (hopen : PicRankOneOpen.IsOpen (divRepAffP1Map C))
   330	    {K : Type u} [Field K] [Algebra k K]
   331	    (mu : pic0Subgroup C (overSpec k K)) :
   332	    ∃ (a : PicRankOneTranslatorIndex (C := C))
   333	      (x : (overSpec k K).left ⟶
   334	        (divRankOneOpenOver (divRepAffP1Map C)
   335	          (divRankOneOpenDataOfPicRankOneOpen (divRepAffP1Map C) hopen)).left),
   336	      (picRankOneTranslatedChart (C := C)
   337	          (divRankOneOpenDataOfPicRankOneOpen (divRepAffP1Map C) hopen) a).app
   338	        (op (overSpec k K).left) x =
   339	          (⟨(overSpec k K).hom, mu⟩ :
   340	            (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op (overSpec k K).left)) := by
   341	  obtain ⟨L, hLfield, hkL, hKL, htow, hfin, hsep, d, r, hdeg, hsupp, hmem⟩ :=
   342	    exists_sepClosedTranslated_mem_picRankOneOpen
   343	      (C := C) (divRepAffP1Map C) (divRepAffP1Map_comp C) mu
   344	  letI := hLfield
   345	  letI := hkL
   346	  letI := hKL
   347	  letI := htow
   348	  letI := hfin
   349	  letI := hsep
   350	  let a : PicRankOneTranslatorIndex (C := C) :=
   351	    ⟨chartTwistClass C d.m r.Z, hdeg⟩
   352	  let baseValue : (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op (overSpec k K).left) :=
   353	    ⟨(overSpec k K).hom, mu⟩
   354	  let translatedValue :=
   355	    (sigmaExtensionIso (pic0GenusTranslationIso (C := C) a)).hom.app
   356	      (op (overSpec k K).left) baseValue
   357	  have htranslated : translatedValue.2 = r.rankOneLayer mu.1 d := by
   358	    apply Subtype.ext
   359	    change mu.1 * thetaFamily C (chartTwistClass C d.m r.Z) (overSpec k K) = _
   360	    rw [SepClosedTranslatedDropResult.rankOneLayer_coe]
   361	  have htranslatedMem : translatedValue.2 ∈
   362	      (PicRankOneOpen (divRepAffP1Map C)).obj (op (overSpec k K)) := by
   363	    rw [htranslated]
   364	    exact hmem
   365	  let v : (rankOneLocus (C := C) (pi := divRepAffP1Map C)).obj
   366	      (op (overSpec k K).left) :=
   367	    ⟨translatedValue.1, ⟨translatedValue.2, htranslatedMem⟩⟩
   368	  let e := picRankOneOpenSigmaIso (C := C)
   369	    (divRankOneOpenDataOfPicRankOneOpen (divRepAffP1Map C) hopen)
   370	  refine ⟨a, e.inv.app (op (overSpec k K).left) v, ?_⟩
   371	  change (sigmaExtensionIso (pic0GenusTranslationIso (C := C) a)).inv.app _
   372	      ((picRankOneOpenSigmaIncl (divRepAffP1Map C)).app _
   373	        (e.hom.app _ (e.inv.app _ v))) = baseValue
   374	  rw [e.inv_hom_id_app_apply]
   375	  change (sigmaExtensionIso (pic0GenusTranslationIso (C := C) a)).inv.app _
   376	      translatedValue = baseValue
   377	  exact (sigmaExtensionIso (pic0GenusTranslationIso (C := C) a)).hom_inv_id_app_apply
   378	    _ baseValue

   380	/-! ## Pointwise coverage and representability -/
   381	
   382	set_option maxHeartbeats 800000 in
   383	-- Elaborating the residue-field specialization crosses both sigma-extension dependent fibres.
   384	/-- The translated rank-one charts cover the sigma extension pointwise.  At a point `t`,
   385	restrict the degree-zero class to `Spec κ(t)`, use the exact separably-closed translated
   386	rank-one factorization there, and take the whole residue-field point as the covering source. -/
   387	theorem picRankOneTranslatedChart_pointwiseCoverage
   388	    (hopen : PicRankOneOpen.IsOpen (divRepAffP1Map C)) :
   389	    PointwiseCoverage C (fun a : PicRankOneTranslatorIndex (C := C) =>
   390	      picRankOneTranslatedChart (C := C)
   391	        (divRankOneOpenDataOfPicRankOneOpen (divRepAffP1Map C) hopen) a) := by
   392	  apply pointwiseCoverage_of_residueField (C := C)
   393	  · exact fun a => picRankOneTranslatedChart_isOpenImmersion (C := C) hopen a
   394	  · intro T s t
   395	    rcases s with ⟨b, mu⟩
   396	    let Tbar : Over (Spec (.of k)) := Over.mk b
   397	    let K := Over.testPointField (T := Tbar) t
   398	    let p : overSpec k K ⟶ Tbar := Over.testPoint (T := Tbar) t
   399	    let muK : pic0Subgroup C (overSpec k K) := (pic0TypeFunctor C).map p.op mu
   400	    obtain ⟨a, x, hx⟩ :=
   401	      exists_picRankOneTranslatedChart_fieldFactorization (C := C) hopen muK
   402	    let q : (overSpec k K).left := Classical.choice inferInstance
   403	    have hq : p.left.base q = t := by
   404	      dsimp only [p]
   405	      exact Over.testPoint_base (T := Tbar) t q
   406	    refine ⟨(overSpec k K).left, q, p.left, a, x, ?_, ?_⟩
   407	    · exact hq
   408	    · exact hx.trans (Over.sigmaExtension_map_left_mk p mu).symm
   409	
   410	/-- Over a separably closed field, openness of the rank-one Picard locus gives a scheme
   411	representing `Pic^0`.  This conditional form keeps the geometric gluing argument reusable. -/
   412	noncomputable def pic0_sepClosed_representableBy_of_isOpen
   413	    (hopen : PicRankOneOpen.IsOpen (divRepAffP1Map C)) :
   414	    Σ J : Over (Spec (.of k)), (pic0TypeFunctor C).RepresentableBy J := by
   415	  let h := divRankOneOpenDataOfPicRankOneOpen (divRepAffP1Map C) hopen
   416	  let f := fun a : PicRankOneTranslatorIndex (C := C) =>
   417	    picRankOneTranslatedChart (C := C) h a
   418	  letI : Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology (Sigma.desc f) :=
   419	    isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc_of_pointwise C f
   420	      (picRankOneTranslatedChart_pointwiseCoverage (C := C) hopen)

    11	/-!
    12	# Tensor products over algebraic extensions at finite subextensions
    13	
    14	Elements and equalities in a tensor product with an algebraic field extension are already
    15	defined at finite intermediate extensions.  These are finite-field wrappers around the
    16	finitely generated subalgebra results in `Mathlib.RingTheory.TensorProduct.DirectLimitFG`.
    17	-/
    18	
    19	set_option autoImplicit false
    20	
    21	universe u
    22	
    23	open TensorProduct

    25	namespace AlgebraicGeometry.DatG0

    27	/-- Every element of `K ⊗[F] B` comes from `L ⊗[F] B` for some finite subextension
    28	`L/F` of an algebraic extension `K/F`. -/
    29	theorem exists_finSubext_tensorProduct_preimage
    30	    {F K B : Type u} [Field F] [Field K] [Algebra F K] [Algebra.IsAlgebraic F K]
    31	    [CommRing B] [Algebra F B] (x : K ⊗[F] B) :
    32	    ∃ L : FinSubext F K, ∃ xL : L.1 ⊗[F] B,
    33	      LinearMap.rTensor B L.1.val.toLinearMap xL = x := by
    34	  obtain ⟨A, hA, xA, hxA⟩ := TensorProduct.Algebra.exists_of_fg x
    35	  letI : Algebra.IsAlgebraic F A :=
    36	    Algebra.IsAlgebraic.of_injective A.val Subtype.val_injective
    37	  let L0 : IntermediateField F K := Algebra.IsAlgebraic.toIntermediateField A
    38	  letI : Algebra.FiniteType F L0 := by
    39	    change Algebra.FiniteType F A
    40	    exact (Subalgebra.fg_iff_finiteType A).mp hA
    41	  letI : Module.Finite F L0 := Algebra.finite_of_essFiniteType_of_isAlgebraic
    42	  let L : FinSubext F K := ⟨L0, inferInstance⟩
    43	  exact ⟨L, xA, hxA⟩
    44	
    45	/-- If two tensors over a finite subextension become equal over `K`, they are already equal
    46	after passage to some larger finite subextension. -/
    47	theorem exists_finSubext_tensorProduct_eq
    48	    {F K B : Type u} [Field F] [Field K] [Algebra F K] [Algebra.IsAlgebraic F K]
    49	    [CommRing B] [Algebra F B] (L : FinSubext F K) (x y : L.1 ⊗[F] B)
    50	    (hxy : LinearMap.rTensor B L.1.val.toLinearMap x =
    51	      LinearMap.rTensor B L.1.val.toLinearMap y) :
    52	    ∃ M : FinSubext F K, ∃ hLM : L.1 ≤ M.1,
    53	      LinearMap.rTensor B (IntermediateField.inclusion hLM).toLinearMap x =
    54	        LinearMap.rTensor B (IntermediateField.inclusion hLM).toLinearMap y := by
    55	  have hLfg : L.1.toSubalgebra.FG := by
    56	    rw [Subalgebra.fg_iff_finiteType]
    57	    change Algebra.FiniteType F L.1
    58	    infer_instance
    59	  obtain ⟨A, hLA, hA, hxyA⟩ :=
    60	    TensorProduct.Algebra.eq_of_fg_of_subtype_eq hLfg hxy
    61	  letI : Algebra.IsAlgebraic F A :=
    62	    Algebra.IsAlgebraic.of_injective A.val Subtype.val_injective
    63	  let M0 : IntermediateField F K := Algebra.IsAlgebraic.toIntermediateField A
    64	  letI : Algebra.FiniteType F M0 := by
    65	    change Algebra.FiniteType F A
    66	    exact (Subalgebra.fg_iff_finiteType A).mp hA
    67	  letI : Module.Finite F M0 := Algebra.finite_of_essFiniteType_of_isAlgebraic
    68	  let M : FinSubext F K := ⟨M0, inferInstance⟩
    69	  have hLM : L.1 ≤ M.1 := hLA
    70	  exact ⟨M, hLM, hxyA⟩

    72	/-- A finite family of elements of `K ⊗[F] B` comes from one common finite
    73	subextension of `K/F`. -/
    74	theorem exists_finSubext_tensorProduct_preimage_finite
    75	    {F K B : Type u} [Field F] [Field K] [Algebra F K] [Algebra.IsAlgebraic F K]
    76	    [CommRing B] [Algebra F B] {iota : Type*} [Finite iota]
    77	    (x : iota → K ⊗[F] B) :
    78	    ∃ L : FinSubext F K, ∃ xL : iota → L.1 ⊗[F] B,
    79	      ∀ i, LinearMap.rTensor B L.1.val.toLinearMap (xL i) = x i := by
    80	  classical
    81	  letI := Fintype.ofFinite iota
    82	  choose A hA xA hxA using fun i => TensorProduct.Algebra.exists_of_fg (x i)
    83	  let A0 : Subalgebra F K := Finset.univ.sup A
    84	  have hA0 : A0.FG := by
    85	    dsimp only [A0]
    86	    induction (Finset.univ : Finset iota) using Finset.induction_on with
    87	    | empty => simpa using (Subalgebra.fg_bot : (⊥ : Subalgebra F K).FG)
    88	    | @insert i s hi hs =>
    89	        simpa [Finset.sup_insert] using (hA i).sup hs
    90	  have hAA0 : ∀ i, A i ≤ A0 := fun i =>
    91	    Finset.le_sup (s := Finset.univ) (f := A) (Finset.mem_univ i)
    92	  let xA0 : iota → A0 ⊗[F] B := fun i =>
    93	    LinearMap.rTensor B (Subalgebra.inclusion (hAA0 i)).toLinearMap (xA i)
    94	  have hxA0 : ∀ i, LinearMap.rTensor B A0.val.toLinearMap (xA0 i) = x i := by
    95	    intro i
    96	    have hcomp :
    97	        A0.val.toLinearMap.comp (Subalgebra.inclusion (hAA0 i)).toLinearMap =
    98	          (A i).val.toLinearMap := by
    99	      ext
   100	      rfl
   101	    dsimp only [xA0]
   102	    rw [← LinearMap.rTensor_comp_apply, hcomp]
   103	    exact hxA i
   104	  letI : Algebra.IsAlgebraic F A0 :=
   105	    Algebra.IsAlgebraic.of_injective A0.val Subtype.val_injective
   106	  let L0 : IntermediateField F K := Algebra.IsAlgebraic.toIntermediateField A0
   107	  letI : Algebra.FiniteType F L0 := by
   108	    change Algebra.FiniteType F A0
   109	    exact (Subalgebra.fg_iff_finiteType A0).mp hA0
   110	  letI : Module.Finite F L0 := Algebra.finite_of_essFiniteType_of_isAlgebraic
   111	  let L : FinSubext F K := ⟨L0, inferInstance⟩
   112	  exact ⟨L, xA0, hxA0⟩

   114	/-- The canonical map from a finite tensor stage into the tensor product over `K` is injective.
   115	This is flatness of `B` over the field `F`, expressed through the tensor-product algebra map. -/
   116	theorem tensorProduct_map_finSubext_injective
   117	    {F K B : Type u} [Field F] [Field K] [Algebra F K] [Algebra.IsAlgebraic F K]
   118	    [CommRing B] [Algebra F B] (L : FinSubext F K) :
   119	    Function.Injective
   120	      (Algebra.TensorProduct.map L.1.val (AlgHom.id F B) :
   121	        L.1 ⊗[F] B →ₐ[F] K ⊗[F] B) := by
   122	  have hmap :
   123	      (Algebra.TensorProduct.map L.1.val (AlgHom.id F B) :
   124	        L.1 ⊗[F] B →ₐ[F] K ⊗[F] B).toLinearMap =
   125	        LinearMap.rTensor B L.1.val.toLinearMap := by
   126	    ext x b
   127	    rfl
   128	  have hinj : Function.Injective (LinearMap.rTensor B L.1.val.toLinearMap) :=
   129	    Module.Flat.rTensor_preserves_injective_linearMap
   130	      L.1.val.toLinearMap Subtype.val_injective
   131	  rw [← hmap] at hinj
   132	  exact hinj
   133	
   134	/-- A finitely generated subalgebra of `K ⊗[F] B` factors through one finite tensor stage.
   135	The factorization is an algebra map, so it can be used directly to base-change a cocycle datum. -/
   136	theorem exists_finSubext_fg_subalgebra_tensorProduct_factor
   137	    {F K B : Type u} [Field F] [Field K] [Algebra F K] [Algebra.IsAlgebraic F K]
   138	    [CommRing B] [Algebra F B]
   139	    (A₀ : Subalgebra F (K ⊗[F] B)) (hA₀ : A₀.FG) :
   140	    ∃ (M : FinSubext F K) (f : A₀ →ₐ[F] M.1 ⊗[F] B),
   141	      (Algebra.TensorProduct.map M.1.val (AlgHom.id F B)).comp f = A₀.val := by
   142	  classical
   143	  obtain ⟨s, hsfinite, hs⟩ := Subalgebra.fg_def.mp hA₀
   144	  letI : Finite s := hsfinite.to_subtype
   145	  obtain ⟨M, xM, hxM⟩ :=
   146	    exists_finSubext_tensorProduct_preimage_finite
   147	      (x := fun a : s => (a.1 : K ⊗[F] B))
   148	  let ι : M.1 ⊗[F] B →ₐ[F] K ⊗[F] B :=
   149	    Algebra.TensorProduct.map M.1.val (AlgHom.id F B)
   150	  have hmap : ι.toLinearMap = LinearMap.rTensor B M.1.val.toLinearMap := by
   151	    ext x b
   152	    rfl
   153	  have hsrange : s ⊆ (ι.range : Set (K ⊗[F] B)) := by
   154	    intro x hx
   155	    refine ⟨xM ⟨x, hx⟩, ?_⟩
   156	    change ι.toLinearMap (xM ⟨x, hx⟩) = x
   157	    rw [hmap]
   158	    exact hxM ⟨x, hx⟩
   159	  have hArange : A₀ ≤ ι.range := by
   160	    rw [← hs]
   161	    exact Algebra.adjoin_le hsrange
   162	  have hι : Function.Injective ι := tensorProduct_map_finSubext_injective M
   163	  let e : M.1 ⊗[F] B ≃ₐ[F] ι.range := AlgEquiv.ofInjective ι hι
   164	  let f : A₀ →ₐ[F] M.1 ⊗[F] B :=
   165	    e.symm.toAlgHom.comp (Subalgebra.inclusion hArange)
   166	  refine ⟨M, f, ?_⟩
   167	  ext a
   168	  change ι (e.symm ⟨a.1, hArange a.2⟩) = a.1
   169	  exact congrArg Subtype.val (e.apply_symm_apply ⟨a.1, hArange a.2⟩)
   170	
   171	/-- A finite family of tensor equalities that holds over `K` already holds over one common
   172	finite subextension containing the original stage. -/
   173	theorem exists_finSubext_tensorProduct_eq_finite
   174	    {F K B : Type u} [Field F] [Field K] [Algebra F K] [Algebra.IsAlgebraic F K]
   175	    [CommRing B] [Algebra F B] {iota : Type*} [Finite iota]
   176	    (L : FinSubext F K) (x y : iota → L.1 ⊗[F] B)
   177	    (hxy : ∀ i, LinearMap.rTensor B L.1.val.toLinearMap (x i) =
   178	      LinearMap.rTensor B L.1.val.toLinearMap (y i)) :
   179	    ∃ M : FinSubext F K, ∃ hLM : L.1 ≤ M.1, ∀ i,
   180	      LinearMap.rTensor B (IntermediateField.inclusion hLM).toLinearMap (x i) =
   181	        LinearMap.rTensor B (IntermediateField.inclusion hLM).toLinearMap (y i) := by
   182	  classical
   183	  letI := Fintype.ofFinite iota
   184	  have hLfg : L.1.toSubalgebra.FG := by
   185	    rw [Subalgebra.fg_iff_finiteType]
   186	    change Algebra.FiniteType F L.1
   187	    infer_instance
   188	  choose A hLA hA hxyA using fun i =>
   189	    TensorProduct.Algebra.eq_of_fg_of_subtype_eq hLfg (hxy i)
   190	  let A0 : Subalgebra F K := L.1.toSubalgebra ⊔ Finset.univ.sup A
   191	  have hA0 : A0.FG := by
   192	    apply hLfg.sup
   193	    induction (Finset.univ : Finset iota) using Finset.induction_on with
   194	    | empty => simpa using (Subalgebra.fg_bot : (⊥ : Subalgebra F K).FG)
   195	    | @insert i s hi hs =>
   196	        simpa [Finset.sup_insert] using (hA i).sup hs
   197	  have hLA0 : L.1.toSubalgebra ≤ A0 := le_sup_left
   198	  have hAA0 : ∀ i, A i ≤ A0 := fun i =>
   199	    (Finset.le_sup (s := Finset.univ) (f := A) (Finset.mem_univ i)).trans le_sup_right
   200	  have hxyA0 : ∀ i,
   201	      LinearMap.rTensor B (Subalgebra.inclusion hLA0).toLinearMap (x i) =
   202	        LinearMap.rTensor B (Subalgebra.inclusion hLA0).toLinearMap (y i) := by
   203	    intro i
   204	    have hi := congrArg
   205	      (LinearMap.rTensor B (Subalgebra.inclusion (hAA0 i)).toLinearMap) (hxyA i)
   206	    have hcomp :
   207	        (Subalgebra.inclusion (hAA0 i)).toLinearMap.comp
   208	            (Subalgebra.inclusion (hLA i)).toLinearMap =
   209	          (Subalgebra.inclusion hLA0).toLinearMap := by
   210	      ext
   211	      rfl
   212	    simpa only [← LinearMap.rTensor_comp_apply, hcomp] using hi
   213	  letI : Algebra.IsAlgebraic F A0 :=
   214	    Algebra.IsAlgebraic.of_injective A0.val Subtype.val_injective
   215	  let M0 : IntermediateField F K := Algebra.IsAlgebraic.toIntermediateField A0
   216	  letI : Algebra.FiniteType F M0 := by
   217	    change Algebra.FiniteType F A0

For a finite semilinear action, irreducibility lets one translate finitely many affine neighborhoods to a common nonempty intersection; translating back gives one affine open containing the whole orbit. I’m inspecting the exact action API and asking a proof worker to test this theorem in a separate file, while I continue on the finite-stage side.

    10	# Semilinear actions on schemes
    11	
    12	This is the scheme-level action vocabulary used by finite-Galois descent.  It
    13	matches the API of the quotient engine in the sibling Algebraic Jacobian
    14	project so that engine can be ported without a parallel set of conventions.
    15	
    16	The inversion in `toSpecAut` is forced by contravariance of `Spec` and by the
    17	group law on categorical automorphisms.  `SemilinearGalAction` then records an
    18	action on a scheme whose structural morphism covers this action on the base.
    19	
    20	## Main declarations
    21	
    22	* `AlgebraicJacobian.GaloisDescent.toSpecAut`: the action induced on a spectrum.
    23	* `AlgebraicJacobian.GaloisDescent.SemilinearGalAction`: a semilinear action on
    24	  a scheme over a field extension.
    25	* `SemilinearGalAction.OrbitsInAffineOpen`: the exact geometric condition used
    26	  by the scheme quotient construction.

    29	set_option autoImplicit false

    31	universe u

    35	namespace AlgebraicJacobian.GaloisDescent

    37	section SpecAut

    39	variable (G : Type*) [Group G] (A : Type u) [CommRing A]
    40	  [MulSemiringAction G A]

    42	lemma toRingHom_comp (gamma tau : G) :
    43	    (MulSemiringAction.toRingHom G A gamma).comp

    45	      MulSemiringAction.toRingHom G A (gamma * tau) :=

    52	/-- A group acting on a commutative ring acts on its spectrum.  The inverse in

    54	-/
    55	noncomputable def toSpecAut : G →* Aut (Spec (CommRingCat.of A)) :=
    56	  MonoidHom.mk'
    57	    (fun gamma =>
    58	      { hom := Spec.map
    59	          (CommRingCat.ofHom (MulSemiringAction.toRingHom G A gamma⁻¹))

    73	        Spec.map
    74	            (CommRingCat.ofHom
    75	              (MulSemiringAction.toRingHom G A tau⁻¹)) ≫
    76	          Spec.map
    77	            (CommRingCat.ofHom
    78	              (MulSemiringAction.toRingHom G A gamma⁻¹))
    79	      rw [← Spec.map_comp, ← CommRingCat.ofHom_comp, toRingHom_comp,
    80	        ← mul_inv_rev])

    82	lemma toSpecAut_hom (gamma : G) :
    83	    (toSpecAut G A gamma).hom =
    84	      Spec.map
    85	        (CommRingCat.ofHom (MulSemiringAction.toRingHom G A gamma⁻¹)) :=
    86	  rfl

    89	    (toSpecAut G A (gamma * tau)).hom =
    90	      (toSpecAut G A tau).hom ≫ (toSpecAut G A gamma).hom := by
    91	  rw [map_mul]
    92	  rfl
    93	
    94	lemma toSpecAut_inv_hom (gamma : G) :
    95	    (toSpecAut G A gamma⁻¹).hom = (toSpecAut G A gamma).inv := by
    96	  rw [map_inv]
    97	  rfl

   100	lemma toSpecAut_hom_inv_hom (gamma : G) :
   101	    (toSpecAut G A gamma).hom ≫ (toSpecAut G A gamma⁻¹).hom = 𝟙 _ := by
   102	  rw [toSpecAut_inv_hom, Iso.hom_inv_id]

   105	lemma toSpecAut_inv_hom_hom (gamma : G) :

   111	variable (K L : Type u) [Field K] [Field L] [Algebra K L]
   112	
   113	/-- A semilinear action of the `K`-algebra automorphisms of `L` on an
   114	`L`-scheme.  Each automorphism of the total space covers the corresponding
   115	automorphism of `Spec L`. -/
   116	structure SemilinearGalAction (X : Scheme.{u})
   117	    (f : X ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of L)) where
   118	  act : (L ≃ₐ[K] L) →* Aut X
   119	  compat (gamma : L ≃ₐ[K] L) :
   120	    (act gamma).hom ≫ f =
   121	      f ≫ (toSpecAut (L ≃ₐ[K] L) L gamma).hom
   122	
   123	namespace SemilinearGalAction
   124	
   125	variable {K L} {X : Scheme.{u}} {f : X ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of L)}
   126	
   127	/-- Equivariance of a morphism between semilinearly acted schemes. -/
   128	def IsEquivariant {X' : Scheme.{u}}
   129	    {f' : X' ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of L)}
   130	    (rho : SemilinearGalAction K L X f)
   131	    (rho' : SemilinearGalAction K L X' f') (h : X ⟶ X') : Prop :=
   132	  ∀ gamma : L ≃ₐ[K] L,
   133	    (rho.act gamma).hom ≫ h = h ≫ (rho'.act gamma).hom
   134	
   135	/-- The orbit of a point under a semilinear action. -/
   136	def orbit (rho : SemilinearGalAction K L X f) (x : X) : Set X :=
   137	  Set.range fun gamma : L ≃ₐ[K] L => (rho.act gamma).hom.base x
   138	
   139	/-- The geometric condition required for the finite-Galois quotient to remain
   140	a scheme: every orbit lies in one affine open. -/
   141	class OrbitsInAffineOpen (rho : SemilinearGalAction K L X f) : Prop where
   142	  exists_affineOpen (x : X) :
   143	    ∃ U : X.affineOpens,
   144	      ∀ gamma : L ≃ₐ[K] L, (rho.act gamma).hom.base x ∈ U.1
   145	
   146	/-- A stable open subset of a semilinearly acted scheme. -/
   147	def IsStableOpen (rho : SemilinearGalAction K L X f) (U : X.Opens) : Prop :=
   148	  ∀ gamma : L ≃ₐ[K] L, (rho.act gamma).hom ⁻¹ᵁ U = U
   149	
   150	end SemilinearGalAction
   151	
   152	/-- A stable affine neighbourhood of every point.  The quotient engine derives
   153	this from `OrbitsInAffineOpen` for finite Galois extensions. -/
   154	class HasStableAffineCover {X : Scheme.{u}}
   155	    {f : X ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of L)}
   156	    (rho : SemilinearGalAction K L X f) : Prop where
   157	  exists_stable_affineOpen (x : X) :
   158	    ∃ U : X.Opens, IsAffineOpen U ∧ x ∈ U ∧ rho.IsStableOpen U
   159	
   160	end AlgebraicJacobian.GaloisDescent

name: horizon
description: How to work inside an Archon Horizon workspace — orient from on-disk state, pick the highest-value formalization work, record progress as commits, and coordinate. Load this first; it points to the specialized skills for detail. Editable per workspace.
---

You are working inside an **Archon Horizon** workspace: a place where AI agents
formalize mathematics in Lean 4 across one or more projects. This skill is the
map. It is deliberately short and **you can edit it** (it lives at
`.claude/skills/horizon/SKILL.md` in this workspace) — tune it to how you want to
work. It points to focused skills; load those on demand rather than up front.

## You are a team; the workspace is where teams collaborate

Think of your session as **one team**: you (the lead) plus the subagents you
spawn as your **workers**, with the tools and skills available to you. A
`horizon run` is your team working through its task. Other runs are **other
teams** working in parallel on the *same shared workspace* — one Lean project set,
one roadmap/board, one ledger, one inbox.

You do not manage other teams and they do not manage you. You coordinate through
**shared state**, not meetings:

- **The board (roadmap)** is the shared plan. Keep your items' status/owner/
  milestone current so other teams see what you hold and where it's going.
- **The inbox** is asynchronous messaging + memory across teams (skill:
  `horizon-inbox`): shared notes, per-task private items, and direct messages to
  another team.
- **Commits** are the durable record; reading recent ledger history tells you what
  other teams just produced (skill: `project-git`).

Before you start, be aware of who else is live (see "Is another run live" below).
A short **synchronizer** digest is printed to stderr at the start of your CLI
commands. Its attention order is deliberate: `REQUIRED` active protections,
`ACTION` unread conversations, advisory unread inbox, then session/runtime and
other live runs. Read it; it is how you stay aware without asking anyone. A new
conversation or reply invalidates the digest cache immediately. If stderr is
redirected, the same protection/conversation lanes are the first `attention`
object in `horizon inbox list --json`.

## Orient (pull state, don't assume it)

**Start here:** your prompt says nothing about who ran before you. Usually
somebody did — often minutes ago, often on this same task, and their report was
written for you. Skill: `horizon-start` — one cheap pass that works out which
situation you were launched into (fresh run, hand-off from the session that just
finished, resume after a crash, or outside a run) and what to read for each.

The workspace root is `$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT`; your shell may start in a member
project rather than at that root. The absolute path to this skill is
`$ARCHON_HORIZON_SKILL`. Live state is under
`$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT/.archon-horizon/` and the manifest is
`$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT/config.yaml`. Read what you need, when you need it — via the
`horizon` CLI (invoke it as `"$HORIZON_BIN" …`):

- **Roadmap** — YOUR strategy sketch across *all* projects, kept as a nested
  outline. `"$HORIZON_BIN" roadmap list` renders the indented tree with per-parent
  progress (`active · 3/7 done`); `--focus <id>` shows one subtree, `--max-depth 0`
  the top level only. Structure it: nest sub-goals with `--parent`, keep your
  item's status/strategy current as you work. It doubles as the **project board**:
  set `--owner <team>` (who holds it), `--milestone <label>` (a free grouping tag,
  filter with `roadmap list --milestone <label>`), and pin concrete deliverables
  with `--pin-commit <sha>`. Roadmap commands print a **warning**
  when parent/child statuses disagree (all sub-items done but parent open, or a
  done parent with open children) — nothing is auto-corrected; you decide whether
  to fix it or leave it (it may be intentional). They also warn when too many
  milestones claim simultaneous `active` focus.
- **Tasks** — a specific piece of work, usually the one a human launched and is
  watching. `"$HORIZON_BIN" task …`. Task commands warn when the open queue grows
  beyond the advisory limit or a `running` status looks orphaned.
- **Inbox** — how teams talk across sessions and projects. Leave a note for the
  next session; read what past ones left. `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox …` (skill:
  `horizon-inbox`). Items can be **owned by your task** (private, e.g. your team's
  memory) or **shared with everyone** (the default); read-state is per-team, so
  `inbox list --mine --unread` is your team's fresh queue, and you can
  direct-message another team with `--to task:<id>`. Inbox commands warn when the
  open working set—especially `memory` and `info`—needs review.
- **Inbox attention order** — before edits, inspect all open `protection` items
  (standing constraints, whether read or unread), then open unread
  `conversation` items and reply or mark them read. Other kinds are advisory
  context. In an agent session an unqualified `inbox list` defaults to open items
  and sorts in this order; use an explicit status to audit history.
- **Conversation discipline** — use a conversation only when a reply/decision is
  expected. Search and reuse an open thread before starting one. Its initiator is
  a participant and owns closure: after consuming the answer, add a concise
  conclusion if needed and archive the thread. Reply to human-started threads but
  leave their closure to the human unless asked otherwise (skill: `horizon-inbox`).
- **Blueprint graph** — declaration dependencies and what's proved. `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> …` (skill: `hgraph`).
  Each node is also an **hgraph** file with attached comments/reviews —
  `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> frontier` ranks what to prove next, and node-scoped failure memory
  goes on the node itself (skill: `hgraph`). Before working on a graph node,
  inspect its tags and any `TO CHECK` reason; `TO CHECK` is an attention marker,
  not a mathematical verdict.
- **Memory** — durable facts/dead-ends live in the inbox: read with
  `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox list --kind memory --json`, write with
  `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox add --kind memory --to horizon --body …`.
- **Usage** — your token/cost consumption this session and run, budget headroom,
  and recent rate-limit signals: `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json`. See
  "Pace yourself" below for how to act on it.

## Your session's identity (environment variables)

The harness exports these to every session — read them instead of guessing:

| Variable | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT` | workspace root (use for `--root`-free CLI calls) |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_SKILL` | absolute path to this `SKILL.md` (never resolve it relative to the shell cwd) |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_RUN` | run id (e.g. `0163`) |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_SESSION` | this session's name (e.g. `0002-horizon-T-1`) |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_SESSION_DIR` | this session's directory (transcript, usage.json, report) |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUND` / `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUNDS` | which round this is (0-based) / the run's planned total |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK` / `ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK_TITLE` | the task id / title (full body: `"$HORIZON_BIN" task show "$ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK" --json`) |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_PROJECTS` | comma-separated projects this task spans |
| `HORIZON_BIN`, `HORIZON_GIT` | absolute paths to the CLI and the ledger-git wrapper |
| `HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR`, `HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE` | the workspace ledger repo + its work tree — `"$HORIZON_GIT" …` is shorthand for `git --git-dir "$HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR" --work-tree "$HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE" …` |

## Pace yourself (usage & interruption risk)

Sessions end for reasons you don't control: rate limits, usage caps, budgets.
The defense is NOT to avoid work — it is to make interruption cheap:

- **Commit at every coherent point** (plain git into the ledger, below). If
  `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json` shows low budget headroom or recent
  `rate_limit`/`usage_limit` signals, commit what you have NOW and prefer
  finishing the piece in flight over opening a new front.
- If this is the run's **last round** (`ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUND` + 1 ==
  `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUNDS`), leave the workspace hand-off-clean: commit, update
  the roadmap/task status, and write the report as if nobody continues today.
- Interrupted anyway? Nothing is lost that was committed — the next session
  resumes from the ledger (see "Resuming" below).

## One-shot discipline (important)

This session runs to completion and is **not resumed** — you will not be re-invoked
when a background job finishes. So **run work in the foreground and block on it**
(builds, checks, subagents). Anything you leave running in the background, or leave
uncommitted, may be lost when the session ends. Commit early and often (below).

## Pick the highest-value work

Read the roadmap and the live Lean state, then commit to the most valuable next
piece. A node being large, multi-session, or blocked on missing mathlib
infrastructure is **not** a reason to skip it — start it, build the missing
lemma/definition yourself as project-local infrastructure, and push it as far as
you genuinely can. Prefer ambitious progress over defensive avoidance.

If this session was launched on a specific task, make concrete progress on that
task's REAL objective — don't preemptively pivot to easy unrelated wins because
the objective is large. Leave a concise task comment only for a durable state
change or blocker, not every action. You own the task's terminal status (skill:
`task-status`): set `--status done` only when the objective is FULLY complete;
`blocked`/`failed` if genuinely stuck; set nothing if it's only partly advanced
(it returns to the queue).

## Fresh-context checkpoints

The old Ground pass is no longer a second orchestrator role, but independent
review is still part of convergence. Spawn the **`ground`** subagent at these
checkpoints:

- before marking a multi-step task `done`;
- after every two substantive Horizon sessions on a long-running task;
- immediately after a strategy pivot, a broad workspace edit, or a surprising
  clean/build result.

Give it the task/project scope and ask it to inspect the actual ledger diff,
blueprint graph, Lean state, roadmap, inbox, and reports with fresh context. It
is read-only on source and reports issues/memory; reconcile its findings before
continuing. Use **`work-reviewer`** for a narrow diff/proof audit and **`janitor`**
when the main concern is workspace hygiene. A one-session task may skip the
periodic checkpoint, but must still obtain a fresh-context review before a
terminal `done` claim.

Schedule upkeep even when the last command did not print a warning. On a
multi-session run, dispatch **`janitor` at the start of every second Horizon
session** and before the final report; on a one-session task, dispatch it once
before claiming completion if the run touched roadmap, task, or inbox state.
Record the checkpoint in the report and wait for the helper before continuing.
If `janitor` is unavailable, ask **`ground`** for the same hygiene inspection;
Ground is read-only, so apply or explicitly record its findings yourself.

## Warnings are work

Commands report problems for a reason — never scroll past them. `lake build`
warnings, `horizon graph sync` warnings, roadmap consistency warnings, deprecation
notices from any tool: if your change caused it, **fix it now** (it is part of
the task); if it's pre-existing or caused by the tool/command itself, don't
silently ignore it — record it as a memory item, file an inbox `issue`, or
address it `--to human` when a human decision is needed. A warning that
survives your session should be one you *chose* to leave, with a trace saying
why.

Collection-health warnings are a dispatch trigger, not background noise. When
`inbox`, `roadmap`, or `task` reports an overloaded queue, stale running item,
or status mismatch, pause the proof loop and spawn **`janitor`** with the
workspace scope. Wait for it, reconcile its report, rerun the command, and
record any warning that remains intentionally. Do this at most once for the
same warning in a session; a persistent warning still needs a report or inbox
issue rather than repeated no-op calls.

## Do the work (Lean)

For any Lean edit, load `lean-check` before touching the file and follow its
required LSP loop: query the target with `lean_diagnostic_messages` or
`lean_goal` before the first edit and after each subsequent edit. Keep `lake
build` for the final session boundary or a specifically required kernel check;
LSP is enough between edits and proof obligations. Use the narrowest `lake env
lean` fallback when LSP is unavailable, and do not duplicate that check when the
configured final build covers the same files.

**Do not `grep` for a lemma.** Grep matches names you already guessed; it cannot
find the lemma whose name you don't know, and that is the one that costs you an
afternoon. This workspace indexes every declaration in every project *and* in
mathlib — query it:

| You want | Use | Not |
|---|---|---|
| "does this lemma exist, anywhere?" | `"$HORIZON_BIN" search "<words or name>" --json` | `grep -r` |
| "what's the lemma for this *statement*?" | LSP `lean_leansearch` (natural language) | guessing names |
| "what matches this *type*?" | LSP `lean_loogle` (`Nat → ?a → ?a`) | `grep` |
| "does something in scope close this goal?" | LSP `lean_local_search` / `lean_hover_info` | reading files |
| "what should I prove next?" | `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> frontier` (ranked) | scanning the blueprint |
| "what does this node depend on / block?" | `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> get label:<id>` | reading imports |
| "is the proof right?" | `lake env lean <file>` (narrowest faithful check) | `lean_diagnostic_messages` alone |

`"$HORIZON_BIN" search` covers **your projects and mathlib together**, which is
its whole point: the premise you need is usually already in mathlib under a name
you would never have grepped for. One query costs a second; re-proving an
existing lemma costs a session. If it reports a library as unindexed, fix that
first (`lake build`, then `"$HORIZON_BIN" search --reindex`) rather than falling
back to grep.

Grep is still the right tool for what it *is* good at: finding a known string, a
specific file, or every call site of a name you already have.

- Search before proving — the lemma may already exist. Skill: `leansearch`.
- Use the **Lean LSP MCP** for tight proof feedback, then verify with the narrowest
  faithful `lake` / `lake env lean` check. Skill: `lean-check`.
- Use the DAG to choose and scope work, not just to report it. Skill: `hgraph`.
- When editing blueprint material, follow the house format. Skill: `blueprint-conventions`.
  The blueprint is timeless mathematics, never a formalization journal. Put Lean
  implementation notes, failed tactics, and declaration-specific progress on the
  corresponding hgraph node with `graph add comment`; do not insert
  "Formalization note" paragraphs into blueprint `.tex` files.

## Read the other projects

They are in this workspace for a reason: the same lemma, pattern, or dead end has
often already been worked out next door. `"$HORIZON_BIN" search` spans **all**
projects — an existing construction in another project is a lead, whether you
import it, copy the approach, or read its blueprint. `references/` holds the
original sources (skill: `references`). Staying inside your own project because
the task named it is how the workspace re-derives the same thing three times.

## Delegating beyond your team (ask permission first)

Your normal way to parallelize is **within** your team: spawn subagents/workers
(skill: `subagents`) and dispatch scoped work to them in the foreground. That
needs no permission.
